newsitem.title: India: India rebels kill 14 in rocket attack.
newsitem.headline: India rebels kill 14 in rocket attack.

text.p: Indian left-wing extremists killed 13 policemen and one civilian in a rocket attack on a village police station in southern Andhra Pradesh state on Friday and fled with stolen weapons, police said.

About 35 members of the outlawed People's War Group (PWG) attacked the Sirpuru village police station with rockets, grenades and automatic guns, police officials in the state capital Hyderabad, 260 km (160 miles) from the scene, told reporters.
The PWG is one of many Maoist rebel groups considered part of the Naxalite movement, which started in India in the 1960s among groups who split from the main communist party.
It was first banned in Andhra Pradesh in 1992 but gained a year-long reprieve beginning in June 1995 before being banned again in July of this year.
Before attacking the police station on Friday, the Naxalites shot dead a police officer at his home, police said.
They then headed for the police station in the Adilabad coal mining district. Officials said they used three rocket launchers and grenades to raze the single-storey structure to the ground.
The guerrillas used AK-47 rifles to kill all 12 policemen on duty, as well as a passing civilian. Five people were seriously injured.
The attackers escaped with 17 rifles and ammunition seized from the dead policemen.
It was the second major Naxalite attack on policemen since Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister V. Chandrababu Naidu outlawed the group in July.
On October 7, seven policemen were killed in the state's Warangal district when the PWG triggered a landmine as a police passed by while patrolling by-elections.
The PWG operates throughout the vast Dandakaranya region straddling the states of Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Orissa.
Other Naxalites also operate in the sprawling eastern states of West Bengal and Bihar and the populous northern state of Uttar Pradesh.
Police said Naxalites were behind nearly 800 violent incidents in Andrhra Pradesh this year, resulting in 150 deaths, including 43 policemen. Twelve police stations have been hit.
Andhra Pradesh had a year-long respite from major PWG attacks after former Chief Minister N.T. Rama Rao granted a temporary amnesty in June 1995.
But Andhra Pradesh police have stepped up security measures against the Naxalites since the amnesty was revoked and say nearly 20 of the rebels have been killed in the past five weeks.
Adilabad district is one of the areas of Andhra Pradesh worst-hit by Naxalite violence. The others are Warangal, Nizamabad and Karim Nagar.
